skyline_extract — GEOCAM skyline op

• Data kinds: image2d → signal

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.skyline_extract(image, sky_is_bright=True, smooth=1.5, max_jump=3, jump_penalty=0.5) (to call the implementation directly, import geocam; geocam.skyline_extract(image, sky_is_bright=True, smooth=1.5, max_jump=3, jump_penalty=0.5); from the registry, opsgeocam.get("skyline_extract"))

Usage

Extracts from a photo, by dynamic programming, 1 line giving the row of the sky–terrain boundary for each column → signal (W,).

The same idea as Lie, Lin and Hsu 2005 (*Pattern Recognition*: robust skyline extraction for navigation):

the vertical change in brightness (positive I[v−1] − I[v+1] if the sky above is brighter) is taken as "boundary-likeness", and among continuous paths whose row does not jump by max_jump or more from the neighbouring column, the one with minimum cost is chosen (jump_penalty × row jump). Even if clouds or vertical edges of buildings give locally strong responses, the continuity of the path keeps the real ridge line.

Args:

image: (H, W) float. RGB is converted to grey first.

sky_is_bright: the sky is brighter than the terrain (daytime). False if inverted in night scenes or backlight.

smooth: vertical Gaussian σ [pixels] (noise). 0 disables it.

max_jump: row jump allowed between neighbouring columns [pixels].

jump_penalty: cost per 1 pixel of jump (boundary-likeness is normalised to 0 to 1).

Returns:

signal (W,) float: the boundary row for each column (0 is the top). For images that show only sky, or only terrain, the boundary response is weak and the mean path cost is close to 0, so it stops with ValueError

(it does not silently return a line of noise).
